subject: Edge fortification briefing and isolation artifact delivery (SIG/CAIQ request)
messages:
From: Melissa Jordan <melissa.jordan@acme.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acme.io
Date: 2026-11-02T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Request: security architecture overview for Dedicated/Private (SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for taking this — Acme's security team is preparing the SIG and CAIQ submission for our pilot with Redwood Dedicated. We need a concise security architecture package focused on network segmentation and isolation for both Dedicated and Private deployment options. Specifically we'd like:

- A network diagram that shows control plane vs data plane boundaries for Dedicated and Private (including edge demarcation).
- A short isolation matrix (who can talk to what: external ingress, inter-tenant, control plane admin plane).
- Notes on egress filtering, KMS boundaries, and how KV cache/prefix caching is separated per tenant.
- Any SOC 2 / CAIQ crosswalk notes you can share (even pointers are fine).

Can you let us know ETA for a draft (PDF + a PNG/PNG diagram) and whether you can redline the SIG questionnaire we will send? Deadline is Nov 6 for our internal review.

Appreciate it,
Melissa
Melissa Jordan
Security Program Manager — Acme Corp
melissa.jordan@acme.io

Attachment: request-checklist.txt (stub: 1.2 KB)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Melissa Jordan <melissa.jordan@acme.io>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: security architecture overview for Dedicated/Private (SIG/CAIQ)

Hi Melissa — thanks for the clear list.

We can deliver a focused packet by end of day Nov 3 for your internal review and a final by Nov 5 to meet your Nov 6 go/no-go. Action plan:

1) I attached a draft diagram (edge-fortification-diagram-v1.png) showing the control/data plane split for Dedicated and Private options and the primary ingress paths.
2) Ben has started a segregation matrix (attached as an XLSX draft) that enumerates allowed flows and enforcement points (NW ACLs, service mesh, egress proxies).
3) Kimberly will prepare a short CAIQ/SIG crosswalk note mapping the most frequently asked assertions to our artifacts.

Two quick clarifications before we finalize:
- For "Private", are you expecting an air-gapped on-prem package or a VPC-hosted private instance in your Azure tenant? That changes the deployment boundary callouts.
- Do you want the diagrams annotated with example cloud/provider constructs (e.g., VPC peering, transit gateway) or should they stay provider-agnostic?

Proposed next step: 30-min walkthrough tomorrow (Nov 3) 10:00–10:30 PT to walk the diagram and matrix. If that works for you we'll send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Olga Petrov
Director, Cloud Security — Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Redwood Inference

Attachments: edge-fortification-diagram-v1.png (stub), segregation-matrix-draft.xlsx (stub)

> Two quick clarifications before we finalize:
> - For "Private", are you expecting an air-gapped on-prem package or a VPC-hosted private instance in your Azure tenant? That changes the deployment boundary callouts.
> - Do you want the diagrams annotated with example cloud/provider constructs (e.g., VPC peering, transit gateway) or should they stay provider-agnostic?

Hi Olga — thanks for the quick turnaround.

We are evaluating two options in parallel: a VPC-hosted private deployment in our Azure subscription (preferred) and a runbook for an air-gapped on-prem proof-of-concept (low priority). Please include both variants in the packet; mark the air-gapped sections as optional.

We prefer provider-agnostic diagrams but with a short appendix that maps components to common cloud constructs (Azure AWS GCP labels). That will help our architecture reviewers.

The walkthrough tomorrow 10:00 PT works — I'll accept the invite once you send it.

Thanks,
Melissa

Attachment: acme-sig-extract.pdf (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Melissa Jordan <melissa.jordan@acme.io>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-02T18:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: security architecture overview for Dedicated/Private (SIG/CAIQ) — updated packet

Hi Melissa — attaching a refined packet based on the items discussed. Highlights in the packet:

- edge-fortification-diagram-v2.png: updated diagram with separate lanes for Hosted (Redwood API), Dedicated pools (reserved GPU clusters), and Private (VPC/on-prem). Control plane endpoints (auth, model registry, telemetry) are shown with labeled boundary controls.
- segregation-matrix-final.pdf: concise table mapping flows to enforcement mechanism (e.g., customer VPC ingress -> load balancer + WAF; inter-tenant traffic -> no direct network paths; KV cache per model instance with tenant-scoped keys).
- Short appendix: KMS boundaries (customer KMS for Private, dedicated KMS tenants for Dedicated), and egress policy patterns (NAT egress through managed proxies and customer-controlled egress gateways for Private).

Notes on differences between Dedicated and Private (short bullets included in packet):
- Dedicated: Redwood manages GPU pools; guaranteed tenant isolation at runtime via process-level isolation, tenant-scoped KV caches, and network segmentation at the hypervisor/cluster network layer. Logging and audit events are forwarded to customer sinks when configured.
- Private (VPC-hosted): Customer controls networking and KMS; Redwood runtime runs in customer VPC with the private control plane agreement. For air-gapped on-prem installs we provide an install bundle + guidance (this is additive and will include an on-prem KMS integration pattern).

I've left the SIG questionnaire for your team; if you want us to pre-populate sections we can — please share the XLSX.

I'll send the calendar invite for the 10:00 PT slot now.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Product Security Engineer — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: edge-fortification-diagram-v2.png (stub), segregation-matrix-final.pdf (stub)

Kimberly / Olga — this looks great, thanks.

A few quick asks after scanning the PDF:
- Can you add a one-paragraph statement about model KV cache tenancy and where PII might be stored (if any) — our reviewer asked specifically about cache persistence and TTLs.
- For the appendix KMS notes, can you call out the customer-managed KMS flow diagram for the VPC-hosted Private option? A small sequence diagram would be helpful.

We'll upload the SIG questionnaire to the Drive link you provided and would appreciate it if you can pre-populate the security architecture sections by EOD Nov 4.

Thanks again — see you on the walkthrough.

Melissa
